{{Short description|American mathematician}}
[[File:Guozhenlu.jpg|thumb|right|Guozhen Lu]]
'''Guozhen Lu''' ({{zh|s=陆国振|c=|t=|p=}}; born 1963) is a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Connecticut]]. He is known for his contributions to [[harmonic analysis]], [[geometric analysis]], and [[partial differential equations]].
 
==Education and career==

Lu graduated from [[Zhejiang University]] in [[Hangzhou]], [[China]] in 1983 and earned his Ph.D. from [[Rutgers University]] in 1991. He was a Bateman Research Instructor in the Department of Mathematics at the [[California Institute of Technology]] from 1991 to 1993, an assistant professor in the Department of Mathematics and Statistics at [[Wright State University]] from 1993 to 1997, and an associate professor of the same department from 1997 to 2000 before he moved to Wayne State University. He became a professor of mathematics at [[Wayne State University]] in 2002. He joined the University of Connecticut in 2016 as a professor. Lu has co-organized many international conferences, including the series of the East Asian Conference in Harmonic Analysis and Applications, which is held annually, rotating between China, [[Japan]], and [[Korea]].<ref>{{cite web|title=3rd EACHAA: East Asian Conference in Harmonic Analysis and Applications|url=http://www.comp.tmu.ac.jp/okmas/index0.htm|website=Tokyo Metropolitan University}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=4th East Asian Conference in Harmonic Analysis and Application|url=http://web.yonsei.ac.kr/4eachaa/|website=Yonsei University}}</ref>
Lu is the founding organizer, since the beginning of the pandemic in 2020, together with his past and current PhD students, of the worldwide online seminar "[https://geometricinequalities.com/ Geometric and Functional Inequalities and Applications.]"  

==Awards and honors==

Lu was elected Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]],<ref>{{cite web|title=AAAS Fellows 2023 Class|url=https://www.aaas.org/news/aaas-welcomes-502-scientists-and-engineers-who-join-ranks-fellows?adobe_mc=MCMID%3D79403441136612548860437381766826318877%7CMCORGID%3D242B6472541199F70A4C98A6%2540AdobeOrg%7CTS%3D1713458335|website=American Association for the Advancement of Science}}</ref> class of 2023, and elected to the [[Connecticut Academy of Arts and Sciences]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Connecticut Academy of Arts and Sciences|url=https://caas.yale.edu/membership|website=Yale University}}</ref> class of 2023-2024,  and  to the [[Connecticut Academy of Science and Engineering]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Connecticut Academy of Science and Engineering|url=https://ctcase.org/|website=CASE}}</ref> class of 2025. In 2015 and 2023, Lu was awarded a Simons Fellowship in Mathematics from the [[Simons Foundation]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Simons Fellows in Mathematics|url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/grant/simons-fellows-in-mathematics/?tab=awardees|website=Simons Foundation}}</ref> In 2017, he was elected to the 2018 class of Fellows of the [[American Mathematical Society]], "for contributions to harmonic analysis and partial differential equations, and for service to the mathematical community."<ref>{{cite web|title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society|url=http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|website=American Mathematical Society}}</ref> The [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] named him to their 2025 Class of AWM Fellows.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://awm-math.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/AWM-News-Nov-Dec-2024-WEB.pdf|magazine=AWM News|date=November–December 2025|title=The AWM Fellows Program|page=8|volume=54|issue=6}}</ref> Lu was elected in March 2026 as an honorary member of [[Phi Beta Kappa]].<ref>{{cite web|title=UConn chapter elects Honorary Member to PBK!|url=https://pbk.uconn.edu/2026/04/08/uconn-chapter-elects-honorary-member-to-pbk|website=University of Connecticut}}</ref>

==Editorial board service==

Lu has served as an editor of numerous mathematical research journals including
''Nonlinear Analysis'',<ref>{{cite web|title=Nonlinear Analysis Editorial Board|url=https://www.journals.elsevier.com/nonlinear-analysis/editorial-board|website=Elsevier.com}}</ref>  ''Advanced Nonlinear Studies''  <ref>{{cite web|title=Advanced Nonlinear Studies|url=https://www.degruyter.com/view/j/ans|website=Degruyter.com}}</ref> ''Acta Mathematica Sinica'' (English Series),<ref>{{cite web|title=Acta Mathematica Sinica, English Series|url=https://www.springer.com/mathematics/journal/10114?detailsPage=editorialBoard|website=Springer}}</ref> ''Communications on Pure and Applied Analysis'',<ref>{{cite web|title=Communications on Pure and Applied Analysis|url=https://www.aimsciences.org/cpaa/editorialboard|website=American Institute of Mathematical Sciences}}</ref> ''Journal of Pseudo-Differential Operators and Applications'',<ref>{{cite web|title=Journal of Pseudo-Differential Operators and Applications|url=https://www.springer.com/journal/11868/editors|website=Springer.com}}</ref> ''The Journal of Geometric Analysis'',<ref>{{cite web|title=The Journal of Geometric Analysis|url=https://link.springer.com/journal/12220/editorial-board}}</ref> and ''Bulletin des Sciences Mathématiques'', also known as the ''Darboux Journal'', founded by Guston Darboux in 1870.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bulletin des Sciences Mathématiques|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/bulletin-des-sciences-mathematiques|website=sciencedirect.com}}</ref>

Since January 2022, Lu has served as the Editor-in-Chief of ''Advanced Nonlinear Studies'' (De Gruyter).<ref>{{cite web|title=Advanced Nonlinear Studies|url=https://www.degruyter.com/journal/key/ans/html?lang=en|website=Degruyter.com}}</ref>   Since 2023, Lu serves as Editor-in-Chief of the book series  ''de Gruyter Studies in Mathematics''.<ref>{{cite web|title=de Gruyter Studies in Mathematics|url=https://www.degruyter.com/serial/gstm-b/html|website=Degruyter.com}}</ref> As of 2024, Lu is the Editor-in-Chief of ''Forum Mathematicum''.<ref>{{cite web|title=Forum Mathematicum|url=https://www.degruyter.com/journal/key/form/html|website=Degruyter.com}}</ref>

==Community service==

Lu has served as a member of the [[Michigan]] governor's advisory council on Asian Pacific American Affairs from 2005 to 2009,<ref>{{cite web|title=Governor Granholm Makes Appointments, Reappointments|url=http://www.michigan.gov/formergovernors/0,4584,7-212-57648_21974-130450--,00.html|website=Michigan.gov}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Governor Granholm Announces Appointments, Reappointments|url=http://www.michigan.gov/formergovernors/0,4584,7-212-57648_21974-195499--,00.html|website=Michigan.gov}}</ref> and as a commissioner of Michigan Asian Pacific American Affairs Commission from 2009 to 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Governor Granholm Announces Appointments to Asian Pacific American Affairs Commission|url=http://www.michigan.gov/som/0,4669,7-192-26847-212752--,00.html|website=Michigan.gov}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Governor Appointments|url=http://www.senate.michigan.gov/rulesandappts/governorappointments.html|website=Michigan.gov}}</ref>
